title: God of Our Lives, Thy Various Praise
description: God of Our Lives, Thy Various Praise in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Ottiwell Heginbotham wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 890 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “New Year. Providential Goodness”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God of our lives, thy var-ious praise Our voi-ces shall re-sound: Thy hand di-rects our fleet-ing days, And brings the sea-sons round.

lines: God of our lives, thy various praise
Our voices shall resound:
Thy hand directs our fleeting days,
And brings the seasons round.
To thee shall grateful songs arise,
Our Father and our Friend,
Whose constant mercies from the skies
In genial streams descend.
In every scene of life, thy care,
In every age, we see;
And constant as thy favors are,
So let our praises be.
Still may thy love, in every scene,
In every age, appear;
And let the same compassion deign
To bless the opening year.
If mercy smile, let mercy bring
Our wandering souls to God:
In our affliction we shall sing,
If thou wilt bless the rod.

licence: Public domain: Ottiwell Heginbotham died in 1768.
credits: Words by Ottiwell Heginbotham (1744–1768), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
